item.title: Pokemon Studio's Next Game Is Now Official
item.description:
A new game is coming from Game Freak, the studio best known for Pokemon games, called Ame no Chi Hare Onna , or Rainy Day, Sunny Girl in English. The new title is a departure from the Pokemon formula, and features an interesting real-world connection players will need to take into account when playing.

While there are always new Pokemon games in production from Game Freak, the studio has created a number of other titles, as well. The most recent of these is Beast of Reincarnation , which released earlier in 2026. Beast of Reincarnation took a far more gritty and epic direction than standard Pokemon games, but Rainy Day, Sunny Girl looks to do the opposite, with a strong anime aesthetic and overall cute concept.

Game Freak Officially Announces New Pokemon 30th Anniversary Release

Game Freak confirms an upcoming release for December 2026 in honor of Pokemon's 30th anniversary.

6
By Joshua Duckworth

Rainy Day, Sunny Girl Combines Magical Girls and Weather

Ame no Chi Hare Onna , aka Rainy Day, Sunny Girl , is an upcoming mobile game for iOS and Android devices that mashes up magical girls with weather conditions. The game's concept revolves around a group of magical weather girls who can transform with the help of companion creatures called Kumorin. These girls are tasked with destroying garbage in the city, which, if left alone, transform into sentient monsters called Yamikumo. The game utilizes real-time weather data from the real world, which alters and boosts the abilities of the girls. For example, sunny days or rainy days can boost different characters' magic. The director of the wildly popular Pokemon Pokopia , Shigeru Ohmori, will lead the new game.

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

Round 1

Which one doesn't belong?

0 / 10
10.0 s

Results

0/5

Best: 0/5

—

More Games

A number of characters in the main cast have already been revealed for the game. Himawari Haruto is the lead character, who is joined by Kumorin partner Arai Pon, a raccoon dog. Yuri Amanohara acts as Himawari's ally, and fights with the help of her own Kumorin, Kon Oribe, a fox. Meanwhile, Izu Shinotsuki is one of the game's rain girls, who is apparently in some kind of conflict with the aforementioned duo. Two other girls have also been teased, including Nono Amamiya, and Emma Ariane, an exchange student from the UK. Their exact abilities are unclear, but Emma appears to be associated with lightning conditions.

Curiously, the game also includes a laundry element that players will need to take into consideration. The cast of characters has multiple outfits they can wear, which will need to be swapped out, as they get dirty over time when worn. After the clothes are cleaned, they need to be hung up to dry, and the weather plays a role here too, as they'll finish drying more quickly on sunny days. Much about the game is still unknown, but it's scheduled to release during Winter 2026. The Game Freak booth at Tokyo Game Show will be highlighting the game, as well.

Pokemon Studio's Next Game Is Now Official
Lies of P Sequel Name Leaked By Official Trademark
Valve Officially Reveals Steam Frame Price and Sales Date
New Open World Stardew Valley Meets Animal Crossing Game Officially Confirmed for September 2026

Though it might come as news to many gamers in the west, this isn't the first time that Game Freak has produced a mobile game. It's previously released titles for both iOS and Android devices since the 2010s, including Pocket Card Jockey and 2025 game Pandoland . However, it's not clear at this time if players outside of Japan will be able to play Rainy Day, Sunny Girl . So far, no release information regarding other territories has been announced.

item.title: PlayStation Just Handed Xbox a Win at a Very Awkward Time
item.description:
Sony hasn't exactly been having a great gaming year, what with active development ending for Destiny 2 , a decision to focus on digital games going into the next generation, and a push for live-service games that are struggling to stick the landing. And it seems that the train of bad news isn't slowing down any time soon for PlayStation , as it was just announced that Kojima's hotly anticipated espionage title, Physint, has been dropped and is now going to be published by Xbox, which puts even more pressure on the blue team as we head into the future.

The dominance of PlayStation in the console market has continued for the last decade or so, and over the past few years, it felt as though Xbox was never going to be able to claw back some of the player base it previously held. However, if we keep seeing poor decisions, questionable moves, and anti-consumer practices, then PlayStation's position may very well be under pressure, especially as we near the end of this console generation where they had felt untouchable for the longest time. It will take a lot for Xbox to reclaim the throne, but I can definitely see a world where a few more stumbles could put PlayStation in a dicey situation in the lead-up to the PS6's launch.

PlayStation Drops Kojima's Next Game, and Xbox Is Stepping In

Amid PlayStation's surprising announcement, Hideo Kojima shares a new statement clarifying the future of his next game and his partnership with Xbox.

By Mohsen Baqery

PlayStation Is Rapidly Losing Ground To Xbox

The gaming industry as a whole has had its fair share of troubles in recent times, but many of the negatives have been offset by a few talented individuals who continue to push the boundaries of the medium. One of the most respected figures in the space, Hideo Kojima, had become a real asset for PlayStation, giving them the Death Stranding series that was met with critical acclaim across the globe. And beyond that, a new project titled Physint was in the works as an exclusive for the platform, but it is now known that the game was on the verge of being axed due to numerous reasons, such as sales concerns from Death Stranding 2 (via Tech4Gamers), and it has found a new home on the other side of the fence with Xbox.

This single decision in isolation doesn't seem that crazy, as it wouldn't be the first project to be pushed aside by a publisher, yet in the context of the rest of PlayStation's recent shortcomings, it feels like a much bigger domino that may very well lead to some serious issues down the line. It's no secret that PlayStation isn't exactly everyone's favorite company right now, what with the decision to end physical production in 2028 and the controversial move to cancel future development on Destiny 2 , and when you start to dig even deeper, the problems start to stack up quite high and have been developing for more than just the last few months.

If we keep seeing poor decisions, questionable moves, and anti-consumer practices, then PlayStation's position may very well be under pressure

For starters, we have to talk about PlayStation's relationship with live-service games, as while Destiny may be the most recent name on the chopping block, their track record is far from clean. You had a Last of Us multiplayer game that was canceled very close to the end of development, a God of War live-service game developed by Bluepoint, a studio which was also just shut down by PlayStation, and perhaps their biggest blunder, Concord, a game that was expected to be the future of the platform that set them back upwards of $400 million.

The list goes on and on, and even if you try to overlook the live-service focus and the controversial hardware changes, it seems as though the cracks are starting to show themselves everywhere, specifically, in PlayStation's exclusive games. There was a lot of hype and build-up to the release of Insomniac's Wolverine , and although it is far from a complete failure, judging by the reviews and reception from the players, I think that people expected more. So, if you see PlayStation spending all this money, time, and energy developing and marketing an exclusive as the next big thing, and it launches as a fairly average game, you start to wonder if it is even worth continuing to support the platform down the line or if Team Green is worth a look.

The Next Console Generation Means Everything for Xbox

It has been six years since the Xbox Series X/S dropped, and in that time, the devices have struggled to find homes due to the rampant popularity of the PS5. However, console generations move pretty quickly, and it won't be long before we get to see what's next in the hardware department, with the PS6 and the infamous Project Helix expected to release before the end of the decade. So if you're an Xbox right now, and you see PlayStation losing goodwill and floundering with their exclusive titles, as well as axing one of the most respected creators in the entire industry, then it makes perfect sense to capitalize on the slump and kickstart the next generation with a bang.

Xbox has already taken some pretty major strides in terms of consumer appeal, most notably with the push for greater Game Pass value by adding day-one exclusives and countless other standout titles. But even outside of their stellar subscription service, it is hard not to look at their upcoming slate and be at least a little bit excited. There's the long-awaited return of Gears of War , several Bethesda games in the works like The Elder Scrolls 6 , and some brand-new IPs such as Clockwork Revolution that all put together make for an attractive lineup for players to get excited about.

Also, to fight back against PlayStation's future no-disc policy, they have announced the Disc to Digital feature, which allows you to insert your existing physical games and claim a digital license for them. While it is unclear right now whether the next Xbox will have a disc drive or not at launch, what this feature does mean is that any discs you buy today will likely be playable on the next generation, and if their backwards compatibility focus continues, then it means your existing library is going to remain relevant for years to come. In the whole grand scheme of things, it isn't a huge step, but much like PlayStation's consistent slip-ups, enough wins or positives like this for Xbox could give consumers a big enough reason to switch sides.

PlayStation Just Handed Xbox a Win at a Very Awkward Time
6 Masterpiece JRPGs That Nobody Officially Played
Fable Makes a Strong Case Against One of the Most Tempting Open-World RPG Shortcuts
Aniimo Release Time & Date

In fairness to PlayStation, Xbox has also had its fair share of internal issues. The mass studio acquisitions and the goal of trying to be everything at once have now backfired, and a series of lay-offs and restructures have brought plenty of bad press for the company. Yet I would still argue there is something to be said about a publisher that is willing to pick up and assist so many different developers, and even if things go wrong, they were at least open to giving it a try. As we look to the future, it is clear that gaming is about to undergo some major changes at all tiers of the ladder, and as the competition gets bigger and the race to the top accelerates, only time will tell if Xbox can finally get the better of PlayStation.

item.title: Lies of P Sequel Name Leaked By Official Trademark
item.description:
SPOILERS AHEAD FOR LIES OF P

Few developers can compete with FromSoftware when it comes to making the best soulslike games on the market, but Nough (developer, formerly known as Round8) and Neowiz came the closest with Lies of P , with the title of its sequel leaking online. Unfortunately, that doesn't necessarily mean Lies of P 's sequel is getting fully revealed soon, but it's definitely tantalizing for fans of the hardcore fairytale soulslike game.

Lies of P recently made the jump to Nintendo Switch 2, and while it's great to see the OG getting continued attention, there's an appetite for more from the world and gameplay honed by Nough. Lies of P is easily one of the hardest Soulslike games in the genre, but in a way that is as punishing as it is fun.

New Soulslike Game on Steam Is a Mix of Bloodborne, Pragmata, and Lies of P

A brand-new Soulslike game on Steam seems inspired by Bloodborne, Pragmata, and Lies of P, but it also carries the DNA of many other iconic IPs.

1
By Mohsen Baqery

Lies of P Sequel's Name Follows Up on Its Ending

As fans know, Lies of P 's ending clearly indicated what would come next, and the new game's title reinforces that. A new European trademark, filed by Neowiz on September 9, 2026, lists a new game called Wonders of O , which follows the title structure of Lies of P. As opposed to Lies of Pinocchio, this title confirms a direct sequel to Lies of P as "Wonders of Oz," following up on the tease of Dorothy. The listing provides little information about what Wonders of O actually is, but it identifies the trademark as "Virtual reality game software," which is a generic classification used for video games. It doesn't mean VR games, for those who are more attuned, and is just a generic classification.

Find the odd one out before the timer hits zero.

Round 1

Which one doesn't belong?

0 / 10
10.0 s

Results

0/5

Best: 0/5

—

More Games

As fans know, Lies of P 's ending comes with a particular conspicuous tease (SPOILER) suggesting that Dorothy from The Wizard of Oz would be the next fairytale/protagonist explored by Nough and Neowiz. After Pinocchio's story reaches its conclusion, the game shows Dorothy's iconic red slippers before she eventually enters Krat, suggesting that she could be at the center of the next Lies of P story. Neowiz did not follow up on that tease in Lies of P: Overture , which instead tells its own story and reaches a separate conclusion.

While there is no official confirmation that Wonders of O is the in-development " Lies of P 2 ," the name immediately calls to mind The Wizard of Oz and its famous setting, while the trademark being filed by Neowiz basically confirms it. Lies of P already established a universe built around reimagined classic stories, so a follow-up centered on Dorothy would fit neatly into the direction the original game appeared to be teasing. The biggest question is what form this sequel will take, as it could go in many directions with The Wizard of Oz 's premise, but it's all but guaranteed to be a soulslike action RPG.

For now, fans will have to wait for Neowiz to say something officially about Lies of P 's future. The studio has not fully announced Wonders of O as a new game, nor has it confirmed that the trademark is connected to a sequel, meaning there is still plenty that remains unknown. But it seems that the golden brick road is at least being built, and Dorothy will soon take center stage in the Lies of P universe.

item.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Distant Shadows Walkthrough
item.description:
Distant Shadows is an optional quest in The Blood of Dawnwalker where Crake, the leader of the Manumits, sends Coen to check up on a beekeeper named Ascar in Tantari. Here’s how to complete this quest and what every choice you can make in it entails.

Forge It Anew Quest Guide In The Blood Of Dawnwalker

Complete Forge It Anew in The Blood Of Dawnwalker—step‑by‑step shard locations, boss tips and where to finish Mihai's sword.

By Nahda Nabiilah

How to Start Distant Shadows in The Blood of Dawnwalker

To start, you have to talk to Crake (Marat) on the lower floor of the Manumits base in Svartrau City after you complete the What Moves the Dead quest.

When talking to him, select the option, “You wanted to discuss something with me” to start the Distant Shadows quest.

There are two conditions you have to meet to get the quest:

  • Complete What Moves the Dead quest.
  • Agree with Crake during What Hunts the Night quest : During the final moments of the What Hunts the Night quest, agree with whatever Crake is saying. Antagonizing him here means that he won’t give you the quest later on.

Infamy level does not have any correlation with whether or not you’ll trigger the Distant Shadows quest.

Distant Shadows Walkthrough in The Blood of Dawnwalker

Go to Tantari by Day

Wait for daytime and head to the settlement named Tantari by following the quest marker. It is located southeast of Svartrau City.

Find Ascar’s Hut

Ascar’s Hut is found in the bottom right corner of the search circle , at the location marked on the map screenshot above. Use focus mode while in the vicinity of this location, and you’ll see a pulsing effect showing a beehive. Follow the pulsing effect to find the property.

Check if Ascar is at Home

Go to the eastern side of the house and activate focus mode to discover an open window you can inspect . Inspect the window to check inside the house. You’ll see Ascar, his dog, and a wooden carving of a horse inside the house. Inspect all three to complete this objective.

Observe Ascar

Follow Ascar from a few feet away, making sure not to get too close. Hide behind the cart in front of Ascar’s hut by crouching next to it while Ascar digs around near the beehive. After a while, Ascar will leave.

Avoid Being Noticed (Optional)

To avoid being noticed, all you have to do is remain a few feet away from Ascar at all times. If you get too close, Ascar will call you out with “Need Something?” to which Coen will reply, “Who me? No, not at all.”

Once this happens, increase your distance from Ascar or hide behind something to make him ignore your presence.

If you do not complete the "Avoid Being Noticed" optional task and walk right up to Ascar, you’ll trigger the final dialogue sequence of the Distant Shadows quest with Ascar. This is not a fail condition. In fact, this is a way to end the quest early. The rewards you obtain won’t change, and neither will the outcome of this quest.

Inspect Ascar’s Hut (Optional)

Go inside Ascar’s hut through the front door. Walk up to the dog, and a cutscene will trigger where you get two options:

  • Feed the dog: Coen gives a piece of meat to the dog, distracting it while remaining hidden.
  • Shoo the dog away: Ascar gets alerted to Coen’s presence by the dog’s barking and comes barging in.

Even if you shoo the dog, the quest will not fail; you’ll only skip to the final part: returning to Marat. However, you won’t be able to follow Ascar anymore.

Inspect the Beehive (Optional)

After leaving his house, Ascar will crouch down next to a nearby beehive for a short while, doing something suspicious. After he leaves, activate focus mode to find the bee smoker near the beehive.

Interact with the beehive and use the smoker to chase the bees away. Then, select the “look inside the beehive” option. Coen will reach in and pull out 25 Denarius (coins), presumably Ascar’s hidden stash.

If you don’t use the bee smoker, Coen will take a small amount of damage from getting stung by bees, but he’ll still be able to retrieve the money from the beehive.

Talk to the Woman (Optional)

Follow Ascar and hide behind the highlighted barrels by the side of the road to listen in on his conversation with a woman. After giving something hidden to the woman, he’ll continue onward.

If you talk to the woman, Coen will ask her about what she was doing with Ascar. You will get three dialogue options:

  • I can make it worth your while.
  • I am with the manumits. You can trust me.
  • Sorry for the bother.

The last option ends the conversation, but if you select either of the first two, you’ll get another two dialogue options:

  • Spare me the empty threats. What did Ascar give you?
  • Right. I’d better go then.

If you select the first option, the woman will yield and tell you that Ascar gave her a jar of honey to give to her children.

Follow the Snares

Continue following Ascar until he heads into the woods, where he has set up a series of snares . There is nothing in any of the snares, but you can use them as markers to know where Ascar is going.

Find a spot to hide

Eventually, Ascar will enter a large clearing, and the quest will update to say “Find a spot to hide.” Look for a tree on the edge of the clearing , highlighted in gold in focus mode vision, and approach it to trigger the end of the quest.

All Quest List In The Blood of Dawnwalker

There are plenty of things to do in The Blood of Dawnwalker, as evident by the plethora of quests in the game's quest list.

By Nahda Nabiilah

Should You Stay Silent or Stop the Soldiers Attacking Ascar?

In the clearing, Ascar will be confronted by a couple of Brencis’s soldiers looking for a payout. They’ll press Ascar about giving away the honey to his neighbors instead of as tribute to them, beating him up in the process. Coen can intervene at four different points during this interaction in the form of timed decisions. At every point, you’ll have two options:

  • Intervene and stop the soldiers from harassing Ascar.
  • Stay hidden.

If you stop the soldiers , Ascar will be mildly thankful, but you’ll be forced to have a conversation with him. If you tell him about the Manumits, he’ll say he doesn’t know what that has to do with him. If you tell him about Marat/Crake, he’ll be livid, and the conversation will end. If you stay mysterious, nothing will happen.

If you stay hidden for the entire encounter, the soldiers will leave on their own, and Ascar will remain in the clearing. You can then choose to either talk to him (same outcome as above), or leave and report to Marat, leaving Ascar none the wiser.

Regardless of what you choose, this decision does not change the outcome of the quest in any major way.

Return to Marat

Go back to the Manumits' hideout and talk to Marat/Crake to finish the quest.

  • If you talked to Ascar at any point during the mission, Crake will be angry that you did, but nothing else will come of it.
  • If you didn’t talk to Ascar , Crake will receive the news about his whereabouts without any extra fanfare.

Regardless of what happened in the quest, you will get to ask Crake about who Ascar really is to him. Crake will then leave in a huff, and Drogos will approach you soon afterward, telling you that Crake likes to go to a certain spot outside Svartrau City to clear his head. You can then choose two options:

  • I’ll go talk to him.
  • I’ll leave him be.

If you choose the first option, you’ll automatically start the “A Closer Look” quest (Crake romance quest). However, if you choose to leave him be, you won’t get this quest for the remainder of the playthrough.

For completing Distant Shadows, you'll receive 500 XP and 1 Skill Point .

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Has a Simple Answer to One of Its Most Divisive Changes
item.description:
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 has finally received a deeper look via the franchise's 40th anniversary Direct, and while fans like myself were thoroughly pleased with what we saw, the reception hasn't been all sunshine and rainbows. I, for one, was over-the-moon excited about getting to play one of my all-time favorite classics on modern hardware, now with overhauled visuals and a handful of quality-of-life improvements many of us have wanted over the last few decades. However, others seemingly haven't been quite as ecstatic as I am about the whole thing, seeing the Ocarina of Time remake as almost too faithful of a remake, with the same gameplay and overall structural design of the original game.

There is one major change, though, that separates the remake from the original N64 classic, and it goes far beyond a mere quality-of-life update. It's a change that, to be honest, I didn't expect to be as divisive as it is, simply because it won't be changing or interrupting the normal flow of gameplay at all. But alas, it is 2026, and it seems like gamers are just getting increasingly dissatisfied with what is, by and large, one of the most enjoyable forms of interactive entertainment there is. And because of that growing discontentment, we have become deeply upset that the Ocarina of Time remake would dare add full voice acting to the game's cutscenes. And not just voice acting, either—but the kind of voice acting that some have come to despise. Even so, there's a simple fix for it, if Nintendo even cares to implement it.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Map Officially Revealed

Nintendo is giving fans a first look at the revamped map of Hyrule within the upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

2
By Michael Brandon Ingram

Ocarina of Time Doesn't Have to Make Players "Suffer" Its Voice Acting

I will admit, I'm a bit naive when it comes to controversy, as I'm almost always on the more positive side of the aisle, even when it isn't a game I'm particularly interested in. Unless I'm reviewing a game, and I am specifically tasked with being critical, my opinion is usually very optimistic, to the point that I can get hyped about a game that I barely knew existed or normally wouldn't have cared about. That's why I'm a bit baffled that there's such an upset about Ocarina of Time 's new voice-acted cutscenes, because to me, it's really not that big of a deal. If anything, voice acting builds a bridge between the veteran fans of the original N64 game and any potential newcomers in the late 2020s, as modern gamers seem to prefer more cinematic experiences.

Put the consoles in the correct order.

Category

Order the selected consoles from lowest to highest.

Your Order

Results

—

—

—

More Games

That's somewhat beside the point, though, because this isn't really about whether adding voice acting to Ocarina of Time 's cutscenes is worth griping about. In fact, that's only half the point, because the real argument lies in just how polarizing this decision is. Players like me have no problem with it, while others most certainly do. And it's not really just the addition of voice acting that some have taken up issues with, but the kind of voice acting it is.

User jayvancealot on Reddit, for instance, said they "simply despise this breathy anime voice acting that is so popular now in dubs," using the Ocarina of Time remake as a reference point. What's interesting, though, is that they also said "I always prefer dubs," which just reinforces my point that modern gamers tend to prefer more cinematic experiences, where the characters feel like actual characters rather than walking dialogue boxes. Still, plenty of comments below the main post seemed to agree with the OP, chiming in with their two cents about what modern English dubs do for classic, once-silent games.

If anything, voice acting builds a bridge between the veteran fans of the original N64 game and any potential newcomers in the late 2020s, as modern gamers seem to prefer more cinematic experiences.

I will say that someone in that Reddit thread brought up a great point that I didn't quite consider before. User Deep-Exit1594 said, "Also the sound effects when you click through dialogue particularly in some of the more solemn scenes adds something I can't quite describe." As soon as I read that, I immediately understood what they meant. There are so many cinematic moments in the original Ocarina of Time that gain a lot of their impact from the silence, like the scene where young Link first leaves Kokiri Forest and is stopped by Saria at the last minute. I can still hear the gravity of that moment in its quietness, and I can see how adding voice acting to it could lessen its impact.

Does that make me upset that Nintendo decided to implement fully voiced cutscenes? Absolutely not. For one thing, I haven't seen enough of the remake yet to know whether the addition of voice acting actually "ruins" the experience. But for another, I prefer when characters are voiced now, too, though I'm not opposed to reading text either. The only time I really find it difficult to get behind voice acting is when it is truly terrible, but even then, if the overall experience has the story and gameplay to justify enjoying it, I will. However, I know I'm far from the only person here to please, and if Nintendo really does want to ensure the Ocarina of Time remake reaches a bit further than me, it might need to incorporate one final change.

Ocarina of Time Could Just Let Players Turn the Voice Acting Off

The obvious solution here is so simple that I almost feel silly spelling it out. Nintendo could just give players the option to turn the voice acting off. Keep the subtitles exactly as they are, let the dialogue play out the way it did in the original game, and suddenly, both sides of this argument get what they want. Players like me who are perfectly happy hearing these characters speak for the first time can leave the voices on, while anyone who believes the silence was part of Ocarina of Time 's identity can experience those scenes without them. Considering how committed this remake otherwise appears to be to preserving the original game's structure and feel, an option like that would make a lot of sense.

Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Has a Simple Answer to One of Its Most Divisive Changes
Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is Facing the Hardest Part of Bringing Back a Classic
Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Gives Official First Look at the Temple of Time
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Map Officially Revealed

More importantly, I don't think giving players that choice would somehow undermine Nintendo's decision to add voice acting in the first place. The voices would still be there for newcomers, and they would still be the default experience if Nintendo wanted them to be. A toggle would simply acknowledge that Ocarina of Time means different things to different generations of players. For some of us, those quiet cutscenes have been burned into our memories for nearly three decades, right down to the little sounds that accompany each line of dialogue. If preserving that experience is as easy as adding one setting to the options menu, I can't see much reason not to do it.
